key_insight: Approximate unitary designs do not just match moments—they can quantitatively approximate the full output-probability distribution, with accuracy improving dramatically when extra local invariance is present.
engineering_relevance: For quantum hardware and randomized benchmarking workflows, this gives a principled way to predict how closely random circuits emulate Haar-random behavior and when moment-based synthesis is sufficient.
method: Proved Kolmogorov-distance bounds between single-output probabilities from strong \(\varepsilon\)-approximate unitary \(k\)-designs and the finite-dimensional Porter-Thomas distribution.
Showed the bound is optimal up to constants, so moment matching alone cannot guarantee substantially better uniform distributional accuracy.
Added local translation invariance assumptions to obtain exponentially better error scaling in \(k\), including total variation guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports explicit worst-case theoretical error bounds: \(O(\sqrt{2^n/(k(k+2^n))}+\varepsilon)\) for general designs and \(2^{-\Omega(k)}+O(\varepsilon)\) with local invariance.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees require additional symmetry beyond approximate \(k\)-design structure, so a circuit that matches moments may still fail to approximate full output distributions well.
paper_title: Random Quantum Circuits Beyond Moment Matching
